probe.note: Five neutral probe solves (weighted sum, no floors) of the actual design problem; values are achieved, feasible designs. Ranges are indicative, not exhaustive.

justification.normalisation: Runtime spans the physical ~41 h floor to the 62 h best probe, siren is scaled from the 3 h requirement up to the 3.14 h best probe, voice from ~70 (acceptable) to 90 (best plausible), and L5 from 0.05 to 0.30, matching the probe ranges without favouring any objective.
justification.scalarisation: Achievement (Tchebycheff) is chosen because the probe set (runtime vs. L5 vs. siren) shows a non-convex trade-off that a weighted sum could miss.
justification.aspiration: Each aspiration sits at or just above the best single-probe value achieved (runtime 62.3 and siren 3.14 from the runtime and siren probes, voice 77.7, L5 0.267), with the ~60 h marketing target and a 0.25 L5 point that lies between the equal probe (0.174) and the L5 probe (0.267).
justification.objective_floors: The 3-hour siren endurance is a stated program requirement, and the siren probe (3.14 h) shows it is reachable, while the 60 h runtime and 'good' voice and 'strong' L5 are goals with no hard numeric limit, so they remain soft.
justification.weights: L5 and runtime carry the most weight (0.30 each) because the probes show they conflict most sharply and both are program goals, siren is weighted lower (0.20) because its 3 h floor is already enforced as a hard constraint, and voice gets 0.20 because its achieved range is narrow (74.6 to 77.7).
